title: Why Amazon warehouses look like chaos on purpose

scenes.text: Amazon's warehouses are a mess. On purpose. A phone case, next to a cookbook, next to a dog toy.
It's called random stow. Items go into whatever bin has space.
Risky? Not really. Computers track the exact bin of every single item.
Here's the clever part. The same product sits in many bins, so the system grabs whichever copy is closest. Less travel, faster orders.
It can even keep look-alike items apart, so pickers don't grab the wrong one.
In 2012, Amazon bought Kiva Systems for seven hundred seventy-five million dollars. Its robots lift entire shelves and bring them to workers.
In July 2025, Amazon announced its one millionth robot, plus an AI called DeepFleet that makes them travel ten percent more efficiently.
So it's not chaos. It's a system.
